subject: Renewal planning: usage forecast, smoothing credits, and re-tiering options
messages:
From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Renewal planning: usage forecast vs committed tiers

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the run of the numbers last quarter. As we start to prepare for our renewal, a couple of points popped up on our side that I want to surface early:

- Actual hosted API usage for Q3 was ~35% below the commit we signed, largely because we paused a major feature rollout until H1 next year.
- We expect a phased reactivation (ramping through Q1), but the profile is uncertain; our finance team wants a smoothing option rather than a hard true-up in the first quarter after renewal.

Around Nov 15 we need to lock a renewal structure. Could we look at options for a temporary rightsize (rebase commit for 3–6 months) plus a smoothing credit or carry-forward mechanism? Wed also like clarity on how per-token thresholds would reapply if we move tiers mid-term.

Ive attached a CSV export of Q3 usage and a short forecast our product team sketched out. Can we schedule a 30-min call next week to go over 2–3 concrete options youd recommend?

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Head of Platform Integrations, Nimbus Health
Attachments: Q3_usage_export.csv (attachment stub)

2) Propose an actionable set of options (short-term rebasing, smoothing credits, or carry-forward credit mechanics) with clear line items for procurement

I can do a 30-min slot on Tue 11/2 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 11/3 09:00–09:30 PT. Which works?

Thanks — talk soon.

marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Nimbus renewal — internal thread / numbers

Team —

Attached is Sarah's CSV (saved as forecast_v3.csv) and the Q3 export. Key points I pulled out:
- Nimbus committed to a 12-month hosted API commit last renewal (baseline commit ~ $300k / mo equivalent in token units).
- Their Q3 realized usage averages ~65% of committed; they expect phased ramp in Q1.

Suggested options to model for the call:
A) Rebaseline: reduce the committed token floor by 30% for the first 3 months of the renewal, then auto-step up to 85% of prior commit over next 3 months. No change to per-token banding; full price protection thereafter.
B) Smoothing credits: keep committed tier unchanged but apply a smoothing credit equal to 15% of unused commit in Q1 as a one-off credit against invoices (not cash refund). Credits would expire after 6 months.
C) Bridge + carry-forward: allow a short-term rightsize (60–90 days) and carry-forward any unused commit as credit applied to the following quarter, with a cap of 25% carry-forward.

Considerations:
- Finance will push to treat credits as line items on the invoice (theyre unlikely to accept opaque 'manual adjustments').
- Legal wants any carry-forward to have an explicit expiration and no automatic renewal of reduced commit.

Can Aditya run an E2E cost/latency risk check if we take the rebaseline route? Karthik — can you sketch the pricing impact and whether we can offer a 15% smoothing credit without opening precedent risk for other renewals?

Ill take the call with Sarah next Wed (11/3 09:00 PT).

—
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbus renewal — internal thread / numbers

Quick notes from my side after a light systems check:
- Short-term rebaseline (option A) is straightforward operationally; autoscaling and capacity routing can honor a temporary lower guaranteed capacity and auto-increase on the scheduled step-up.
- Smoothing credit (option B) is easiest from a billing perspective if we push it as a distinct "Credit Line: Q1 Smoothing" row on the invoice. That meets their finance ask.
- Carry-forward mechanics (option C) are fine but we should cap at 25% and set 6-month expiry to limit liability.

Attached: proposed_pricing_nimbus_v2.pdf (pricing table + per-token thresholds & a sample invoice line) — I recommend going to Sarah with B as the primary option and A as the fallback if they insist on a lower immediate cash commitment.

If legal wants wording, I can draft a short amendment template for the invoice credit and carry-forward clause.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_pricing_nimbus_v2.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@nimbushealth.com>

Thanks — the proposed approach sounds workable. Nimbus prefers option B (smoothing credit shown as a discrete invoice line) with a 15% credit applied to realized under-usage in Q1, and a 6-month expiration on any carry-forward (if we end up using C).

Two asks before we sign:
1) Please send an updated quote/contract language with the invoice line item explicitly called out so our procurement can see it on the face of the SOW.
2) Can you add the DocuSign link and an estimated effective date if we sign by 11/15?

Im attaching our internal PO placeholder so procurement can pre-stage it.

Appreciate the flexibility — talk on Wed.

Best,
Sarah
